html:
The Guaycura were hunter-gatherers of the southern Baja California peninsula, living between Loreto and La Paz in what is now Baja California Sur, Mexico. They moved in small bands through a dry land, gathering pitahaya cactus fruit, agave and seeds, hunting deer and small game and taking shellfish on the coasts. Their language is known mainly from Jesuit records.

Their neighbours were the Pericú to the south and the Cochimí to the north. Jesuits built missions in and near their land from 1697, when Loreto was founded, as an outpost of New Spain. Smallpox, measles and the upheaval of mission life cut their numbers fast. A great revolt in 1734, led by the Pericú, burned the southern missions. By the early 1800s the Guaycura had disappeared as a separate people.
